_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `s.stdio.semio.brep` is a semio-NATIVE format that no third party reads or writes, so the reference is a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language, written from this subset's own committed specification documents.

packages.role: OpenCASCADE 8.0 exact-geometry kernel, compiled to WASM

oracles.rationale:
🧊️ THE QUALIFYING REFERENCE FOR ALL THIRTEEN KERNEL MUTATIONS, and the reason this subset no longer rests on a Python reimplementation of its own rules.

What makes it reachable is that this subset's STEP exporter is REAL: it mints a genuine AP214 Part-21 graph — `VERTEX_POINT`, `EDGE_CURVE`, `ORIENTED_EDGE`, `EDGE_LOOP`, `FACE_OUTER_BOUND`, `ADVANCED_FACE`, `CLOSED_SHELL`, `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`, `BREP_WITH_VOIDS` — rather than dumping the artifact's own DSL text under a `.step` extension, which is what 80 serializers elsewhere in this repository still do. An OpenCASCADE kernel can therefore read what these mutations actually produced.

WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT ADJUDICATE, taken from the exporter's own documented boundaries rather than assumed. It CAN judge topology (solid/shell/face/edge/vertex counts, genus, connected components), geometry (volume, area, bounds) and tessellated agreement. It CANNOT judge `BrepShellFace.orientation` or `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D.ref_direction`, which the exporter drops, and it CANNOT judge id preservation, because every export mints fresh sequential Part-21 ids by design — neutral in-memory ids are not an exchange format's identity scheme. Asserting id equality against this oracle would fail correct code, so those three remain the retained second implementation's job.

Engine-family accounting is unchanged from the sibling registration: brepjs and any other OCCT wrapper are ONE family, not two.

productionDebt.plan: 🔒️ MEASURED, NOT FEARED — the plan's shared-kernel-ancestry risk, already realised. `🟦️brep-implementation.ts` imports `brepjs` and `brepjs-opencascade` as the CAD plugin's PRODUCTION exact-BRep implementation, behind the `OwnedBrep*` interface the repository requires of an external library. Two consequences, and they differ per artifact. (1) For `s.cad.cad`, brepjs is NOT independent evidence: the reference and the code under test would sit on the same OpenCASCADE kernel and agree on its defects. `engineIndependenceBreaches` reports exactly that as soon as a CAD subject declares its engine family, so the day someone points a CAD mutation at this oracle is a reported finding rather than a silent weakening. (2) For `s.stdio.step@ap214/✳️cc6` — the owner registering it here — the subject is the pure-Rust STEP codec in `semio-s-plugin-stdio`, which carries no geometry kernel at all, so brepjs remains a genuinely independent exact-geometry reference for THIS subset and its fixture corpus. RETIREMENT: this entry shrinks when the CAD plugin's BRep implementation is either replaced by an in-repository kernel or moved behind a boundary the STEP subsets do not share; it must never grow. The `testOnly` claim on this registration is therefore a TARGET, and the dependency phase prints this debt on every run so it cannot quietly become permanent.

oracles.rationale:
SUPERSEDED AS THE PRIMARY REFERENCE by `brepjs-occt`, and RETAINED as the supplement it always said it was. This entry's own text already recorded that a qualifying third-party reference was still owed; that debt is now discharged by an OpenCASCADE kernel reading the STEP this subset exports. It is kept because a second implementation still catches a class of bug the carrier cannot show — anything the export documents as dropped (`BrepShellFace.orientation`, `ref_direction`, semio ids) is invisible to a STEP reader by construction, and this implementation sees it.

No third-party library reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, so a differential comparison's second PRODUCER cannot be a foreign package — it has to be a second implementation. `🧪️tests/mutate-semio-brep/🐍️component.py` is that implementation: the text envelope, the DSL grammar, the pack frame, both tagged geometry unions, the JSON projection and all thirteen verbs of `SemioBrepMutation`, written in Python from the committed specification documents alone — `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/📝️text/📖️component.grammar.semio` for the record grammar and its `L|C|E|N` curve and `P|C|O|S|T|N` surface tags with their exact field lists, `…/📸️snapshot/💾️binary/📡️component.protocol.semio` for the pack header and the sentence naming its per-collection payload, `…/📸️snapshot/🔣️component.json` for the projection's member names, `…/🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️component.grammar.semio` for the thirteen verbs and their argument lists, and `🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🧬️semio/🦀️component.rs` for the semio envelope. It imports nothing from the Rust it judges and transliterates none of it. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation is the adapter file, so this entry contributes no dependency to `🔒️dependencies.json` and nothing to the import-purity probe. The derivation of the pack layout past the header — which the protocol description names but declines to frame — is pinned by the Python re-encoding the committed `🧊️solid` `🎒️example.pack.semio` byte for byte, a file carrying a line, a circle, a NURBS curve and a NURBS surface, which a misreading could not do.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `semio-v1-brep-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 13-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

probes.rationale: THE MESH HALF OF THE GATE, on engine families the exact kernel does not share — a tessellation check run on the same OpenCASCADE that produced the shapes would agree with that kernel's own defects. It reports TWO independent metrics because they miss different things. (1) The SYMMETRIC-DIFFERENCE VOLUME of the two meshes, `(A \\ B) ∪ (B \\ A)`, computed by manifold's exact mesh boolean: no sampling, no seed, no error bound, exactly 0 for identical meshes. (2) The SYMMETRIC HAUSDORFF DISTANCE via three-mesh-bvh's closest-point queries, evaluated at every vertex of both meshes. A thin spike of negligible volume barely moves the first while moving the second by its full length; a lost internal cavity moves the first while leaving the outer surface — and therefore the second — untouched. brepjs emits one vertex per FACE CORNER, so the probe welds coincident vertices on a fixed 1e-7 grid before handing meshes over: format normalization, with the grid a constant rather than a tunable, because a weld distance a comparison could widen would be a way to make two different solids agree.

qualification.evidence: Measured on this corpus, with both passing and failing demonstrated rather than assumed. THE GATE IS EXPRESSED IN TESSELLATION TOLERANCES, and a first attempt at a bare constant is why: two tessellations of ONE solid differ by their chord error, which is bounded by the tolerance they were built at, so the honest question is not how far apart the meshes are but whether they are further apart than tessellation alone could explain. `cut-sphere-from-box` at tolerance 1e-1 against the same solid at 1e-3 — a 90× triangle-count difference, 398 vs 35 716 — measures a Hausdorff of 0.0903 mm, i.e. 0.903 declared tolerances, while a normalized-constant gate sized for that case would have had to sit at 2e-3, four orders looser than the flat-face cases need. Expressed in tolerances, ONE threshold of 3 serves both. Results: (A) SAME SOLID, DIFFERENT TESSELLATION — flat `cut-bored-box-through` 520 vs 2828 triangles → 3.97e-13 tolerances, symmetric difference 9.80e-05; curved `cut-sphere-from-box` 398 vs 35 716 → 0.903 tolerances, symmetric difference 1.94e-03. Both pass. (B) A DIFFERENT SOLID → symmetric difference 2.11e-01. (C) A LOST INTERNAL CAVITY WITH AN IDENTICAL OUTER SURFACE, the defect mesh similarity is classically blind to → 7.00e+03 tolerances, symmetric difference 2.78e-02, and `genusEqual` false. (D) ONE BODY VERSUS TWO with relative volume error EXACTLY 0.0 → symmetric difference 1.00, `connectedComponentsEqual` false; the case that shows why these metrics are kept alongside volume rather than instead of it. The gate at 3 tolerances clears the worst legitimate tessellation gap by 3.3× and rejects the lost cavity by 2 300×.

comparisonPipelines.description: The thirteen kernel mutations of semio's own b-rep, compared through the STEP carrier its exporter mints. Identical in shape to the sibling `semantic-brep-solid-v1` because the carrier and the questions are identical; what differs is the SUBJECT — there, file-level edits to a STEP document, here, topological edits to semio's own b-rep graph.

stages.description: An independent reader accepts both files.
Scale-normalized exact-shape comparison — the operative equality.
Component count. Face and edge counts are NOT asserted here: two valid kernels may split a periodic surface differently while representing the same solid.
Canonical STEP byte equality. UNQUALIFIED — see the probe's own qualification record. Reports; gates nothing.

🔺️ The mesh half, on independent engine families, and GATING. Different tessellation is allowed; a different solid is not. The Hausdorff bound is expressed in TESSELLATION TOLERANCES rather than as a normalized constant, because two tessellations of one solid differ by exactly the chord error their tolerance permits — measured, a 90× triangle-count gap on a curved cut costs 0.903 tolerances while a lost internal cavity costs 7 000.

fixtureManifests.notes: Moving corner 2 to where corner 3 used to be (and vice versa, by construction) turns a simple square into a self-crossing bowtie. `polygon()` does NOT throw on the in-memory attempt — MEASURED there, its own `measureArea()` collapses to a value indistinguishable from zero, the two triangular lobes' signed contributions cancelling. But this is exactly lesson 1 in miniature: measured OFF `expected.step` — the form a real consumer sees — the picture is different again. OCCT's STEP writer silently splits the self-intersecting single face into TWO separate valid triangular faces meeting at the crossing point (2 faces, 2 shells, 5 vertices — one MORE than the 4 input points, the crossing point itself — 6 edges), whose combined AREA is 50, exactly HALF the original square's 100, not zero at all. Three measurements, three different pictures of the same illegal move: `false`-free in-memory success, a cancelled zero-ish signed area, and a round-tripped shape with real positive area the input geometry never specified. All three are recorded.

fixtureManifests.notes: The exact case this subset's own goal calls out: deleting a face still bounding a closed shell. BEFORE is a complete 6-face box solid. Attempting the deletion by rebuilding `solid()` from the remaining 5 faces — MEASURED — does NOT throw: OpenCASCADE returns a shape immediately (`isValidSolid()` on THAT in-memory object measures `false`), but the honest proof only shows up downstream: exported to STEP and re-imported — the only form a real consumer ever sees — `getSolids()` on it measures `0`, even though it still carries all 5 faces / 12 edges / 8 vertices and `isValidSolid()` on the re-imported shape now (misleadingly) measures `true`. `isValidSolid()` is NOT a reliable signal across a STEP round-trip; `getSolids().length === 0` on the re-imported artifact is. Both numbers are recorded in `expected.metrics.json` rather than only the one that reads cleanly.
